newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition, SPD agree formal pensions talks.
newsitem.headline: German coalition, SPD agree formal pensions talks.

text.p: Leaders from Germany's governing coalition and the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) agreed on Tuesday to hold full-scale negotiations over reforming the state pensions system.
Social Security Minister Norbert Bluem, speaking after two-hour exploratory talks, told reporters "we will try to reach agreement".
In order to cope with the expected explosion of the number of German pensioners, Bluem proposes modest cuts in old-age pay while keeping Germany's pay-as-you-go pensions scheme intact.
The Bluem plan envisages cutting a typical pension to 64 percent of average net wages eventually from 70 percent, while contributions would be cut back from today's record level.

The SPD has, however, opposed any cuts in pensions payouts and its social affairs spokesman Rudolf Dressler said it would be up to his party's executive to decide next Monday whether to join the talks.
"Regrettably, the only revelation of the talks was that the coalition said it was ready to discuss SPD proposals. This is a bare minimum," Dressler said.
